=== tariff header
tariff "Dry van TL"
---
tariff "Dry van TL"

=== library header
library "accessorials"
---
library "accessorials"

=== condition header
condition "Residential delivery"
---
condition "Residential delivery"

=== header after comments
// leading comment
tariff "t"
---
tariff "t"

=== file doc after the header
tariff "t"

/// About this file.
/// Second line.

let x = 1
---
tariff "t"
file doc "About this file.\nSecond line."
let x = 1

=== doc directly above the first item is the item's
tariff "t"
/// The rate.
input rate: Money/mi = $2.35/mi
---
tariff "t"
doc "The rate."
input rate: Money/mi = $2.35/[mi]

=== use a whole module
tariff "t"
use std.fuel
---
tariff "t"
use std.fuel

=== use names
tariff "t"
use std.ltl.{ deficit, Break }
---
tariff "t"
use std.ltl.{deficit, Break}

=== use with a trailing comma over lines
tariff "t"
use std.ltl.{
  deficit,
  Break,
}
---
tariff "t"
use std.ltl.{deficit, Break}

=== use with an alias
tariff "t"
use std.fuel as f
use std.fuel.{ stepPercent } as g
---
tariff "t"
use std.fuel as f
use std.fuel.{stepPercent} as g

=== use from the organisation
tariff "t"
use org.accessorials.{ residential }
---
tariff "t"
use org.accessorials.{residential}

=== input without a default
tariff "t"
input breaks: List<Break>
---
tariff "t"
input breaks: List<Break>

=== input with a default
tariff "t"
input minimumCharge: Money = $450
---
tariff "t"
input minimumCharge: Money = $450

=== const with and without a type
library "l"
const DIESEL_BASE: Money = $3.50
const STEP = 5
---
library "l"
const DIESEL_BASE: Money = $3.50
const STEP = 5

=== private const
library "l"
private const LIMIT: Int = 3
---
library "l"
private const LIMIT: Int = 3

=== type declaration
library "l"
type Break = { from: Weight, rate: Money/cwt, minimum: Money? }
---
library "l"
type Break =
  from: Weight
  rate: Money/cwt
  minimum: Money?

=== type declaration over lines with field docs
library "l"
type Rated = {
  /// The billed weight.
  weight: Weight,
  rate: Money/cwt,
  deficit: Bool,
}
---
library "l"
type Rated =
  doc "The billed weight."
  weight: Weight
  rate: Money/cwt
  deficit: Bool

=== enum declaration
library "l"
enum Zone { A, B, C }
---
library "l"
enum Zone
  A
  B
  C

=== enum with docs and a trailing comma
library "l"
enum Service {
  /// The usual.
  Standard,
  Guaranteed,
  Expedited,
}
---
library "l"
enum Service
  doc "The usual."
  Standard
  Guaranteed
  Expedited

=== enum with capitals variants
library "l"
enum Region { NE, SW }
---
library "l"
enum Region
  NE
  SW

=== function with a block body
library "l"
fn deadhead(empty: Distance, rate: Money/mi) -> Money {
  let paid = (empty - 50 mi).max(0 mi)
  return rate * paid
}
---
library "l"
fn deadhead(empty: Distance, rate: Money/mi) -> Money
  let paid = (call (. (paren (- empty 50[mi])) max) 0[mi])
  return (* rate paid)

=== function with an expression body
library "l"
fn residential(fee: Money = $95) = fee
---
library "l"
fn residential(fee: Money = $95) = fee

=== function with a return type and an expression body
library "l"
fn billed(weight: Weight, to: Weight = 100 lb) -> Weight = weight.roundUp(to: to)
---
library "l"
fn billed(weight: Weight, to: Weight = 100[lb]) -> Weight = (call (. weight roundUp) to:to)

=== function parameters over lines
library "l"
fn detention(
  dwell: Duration,
  free: Duration = 2 h,
  rate: Money/h,
) -> Money = rate * (dwell - free).max(0 h)
---
library "l"
fn detention(dwell: Duration, free: Duration = 2[h], rate: Money/h) -> Money = (* rate (call (. (paren (- dwell free)) max) 0[h]))

=== private function
library "l"
private fn helper() -> Int = 1
---
library "l"
private fn helper() -> Int = 1

=== test block
tariff "t"
test "a heavy load" {
  given shipment.weight = 1_240 lb
  expect total == $511.20
}
---
tariff "t"
test "a heavy load"
  given shipment.weight = 1240[lb]
  expect (== total $511.20)

=== statements at file level are items
tariff "t"
let miles = shipment.distance
charge "Linehaul" = $1
minimum $450
---
tariff "t"
let miles = (. shipment distance)
charge (text "Linehaul") = $1
minimum $450

=== doc on a let at file level
tariff "t"
/// Miles.
let miles = shipment.distance
---
tariff "t"
doc "Miles."
let miles = (. shipment distance)

=== condition final expression
condition "c"
input zips: List<Text> = []
lane.destination.zip3 in zips
---
condition "c"
input zips: List<Text> = (list)
expr (in (. (. lane destination) zip3) zips)

=== stray doc separated by a blank line
tariff "t"
let a = 1
/// Nothing below.

let b = 2
---
tariff "t"
let a = 1
let b = 2
! doc 21..39 This doc comment is not attached to anything; write it on the line right above what it describes, or make it a plain `//` comment

=== stray doc at the end of the file
tariff "t"
let a = 1
/// Dangling.
---
tariff "t"
let a = 1
! doc 21..34 This doc comment is not attached to anything; write it on the line right above what it describes, or make it a plain `//` comment

=== stray doc inside a block
tariff "t"
if true {
  /// Not attached.
  let a = 1
}
---
tariff "t"
if true
  let a = 1
! doc 23..40 This doc comment is not attached to anything; write it on the line right above what it describes, or make it a plain `//` comment

=== private on something that cannot be private
tariff "t"
private input x: Int
---
tariff "t"
private input x: Int
! syntax 11..18 Only a `fn`, `const`, `type` or `enum` can be `private`

=== missing header
let x = 1
---
let x = 1
! header 0..3 A file starts with its header: `tariff "Name"`, `library "name"` or `condition "Name"`

=== empty file
---
! header 0..0 A file starts with its header: `tariff "Name"`, `library "name"` or `condition "Name"`

=== misplaced header
let x = 1
tariff "t"
---
tariff "t"
let x = 1
! header 10..20 The header must be the file's first line

=== two headers
tariff "a"
tariff "b"
---
tariff "a"
! header 11..21 A file has only one header

=== header with interpolation
tariff "a {x}"
---
tariff "a "
! syntax 7..14 A name in quotes can't interpolate values

=== header without a name
tariff
let x = 1
---
tariff ""
let x = 1
! syntax 6..6 Expected the tariff's name in quotes after `tariff`

=== type name written in lower case
library "l"
type myBreak = { from: Weight }
---
library "l"
type myBreak =
  from: Weight
! syntax 17..24 A type's name starts with a capital letter: `MyBreak`

=== type declared as something other than a record
library "l"
type Rate = Money
---
library "l"
type Rate =
! syntax 24..29 A type declaration lists its fields in braces, like `type Break = '{' from: Weight '}'`

=== value name written in capitals
tariff "t"
let Miles = 1
---
tariff "t"
let Miles = 1
! syntax 15..20 A value's name starts with a lower-case letter: `miles`

=== an input with a range constraint
tariff "t"
input rate: Money/mi = $2.35/mi where $0.50/mi..=$15/mi
input stops: Int where 0..
---
tariff "t"
input rate: Money/mi = $2.35/[mi] where (..= $0.50/[mi] $15/[mi])
input stops: Int where (.. 0 _)

=== an input with a list constraint
tariff "t"
input service: Text = "Standard" where ["Standard", "Guaranteed"]
---
tariff "t"
input service: Text = (text "Standard") where (list (text "Standard") (text "Guaranteed"))

=== a property
tariff "t"
property "heavier never bills less" {
  vary shipment.weight in 1 lb..40_000 lb
  vary input.rate
  vary w in [1 lb, 2 lb]
  assume w > 0 lb
  given fuel.price = $3.20/gal
  expect total >= $0
  expect total nondecreasing in shipment.weight
  expect charge(FSC) ?? $0 nonincreasing in w
}
---
tariff "t"
property "heavier never bills less"
  vary shipment.weight in (.. 1[lb] 40000[lb])
  vary input.rate
  vary w in (list 1[lb] 2[lb])
  assume (> w 0[lb])
  given fuel.price = $3.20/[gal]
  expect (>= total $0)
  expect total nondecreasing in shipment.weight
  expect (?? (call charge FSC) $0) nonincreasing in w

=== a property's name must be quoted
tariff "t"
property heavier {
}
---
tariff "t"
expr property
! syntax 20..27 Each statement goes on its own line; start a new line before `heavier`

=== property is a name elsewhere
tariff "t"
let property = 1
let vary = property + 1
---
tariff "t"
let property = 1
let vary = (+ property 1)
